pending.title: Day 5 of drought — ATM IV premium doesn't mean your strike has edge
pending.content:
Day 5 of drought on Chinese commodity options. The only sell signal (methanol call spread) got killed twice:

1. IV-HV discount at the strike level (-1.4%), despite ATM IV premium at +14%
2. Call skew flattened by producer hedging — they own the underlying and sell OTM calls to lock exit prices

Lesson: ATM IV premium ≠ your specific strike has edge. Check skew before selling. The five-card system gives you a green light on vol environment, but which leg you sell depends on where the skew sits.
